issue.title: Service workers aren't correctly located when exporting to non-root paths

labels.name: p2-nice-to-have
labels.description: SvelteKit cannot be used by a small number of people, quality of life improvements, etc.

issue.body:
### Describe the bug

When I build an PWA that I intend to publish to GitHub Pages, I need to be able to tell SvelteKit that the path to the service worker isn't `/service-worker.js`, but instead rebased to wherever my app is located. This is mildly related to #2697, which was fixed by introducing `%svelte.assets%`. Now we need the service worker registration code to respect the app's base path as well.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/illright/sveltekit-repro-basepath

### Logs

```shell
Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Failed to register a ServiceWorker for scope ('http://localhost:8080/') with script ('http://localhost:8080/service-worker.js'): A bad HTTP response code (404) was received when fetching the script.
```


### System Info

```shell
System:
    OS: Linux 5.10 Arch Linux
    CPU: (8) x64 Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-8265U CPU @ 1.60GHz
    Memory: 1.27 GB / 3.76 GB
    Container: Yes
    Shell: 3.3.1 - /bin/fish
  Binaries:
    Node: 17.3.0 - /usr/sbin/node
    npm: 8.3.0 - /usr/sbin/npm
  npmPackages:
    @sveltejs/adapter-static: ^1.0.0-next.26 => 1.0.0-next.26 
    @sveltejs/kit: next => 1.0.0-next.224 
    svelte: ^3.44.0 => 3.45.0
```


### Severity

serious, but I can work around it

### Additional Information

Additionally, it would be nice if `svelte-kit preview` would serve the `build/` directory instead of `build/non-root` (if I set the base path to `/non-root`). As you can see in the reproduction repository, I have to use `sirv` to properly test my application, which makes `pnpm preview` useless for statically adapted projects with non-root base paths.

body:
The issue seems to be with the internal manifest of the workers.

```js
export const manifest = {
	appDir: "_app",
	assets: new Set(["favicon.png", /*removed for brevity...*/,"svg/Youtube.svg","svg/YoutubeRed.svg" /* no service-worker.js :( */]),
	_: {
		mime: {".png":"image/png",".jpg":"image/jpeg",".svg":"image/svg+xml"},
		entry: {"file":"start-d1b74b63.js","js":["start-d1b74b63.js","chunks/vendor-873c0a70.js"],"css":["assets/start-d5b4de3e.css"]},
		nodes: [
			() => import('../output/server/nodes/0.js'),
			() => import('../output/server/nodes/1.js'),
			() => import('../output/server/nodes/2.js'),
			() => import('../output/server/nodes/3.js'),
			() => import('../output/server/nodes/4.js'),
			() => import('../output/server/nodes/5.js'),
			() => import('../output/server/nodes/6.js'),
			() => import('../output/server/nodes/7.js'),
			() => import('../output/server/nodes/8.js'),
			() => import('../output/server/nodes/9.js'),
			() => import('../output/server/nodes/10.js')
		],
		routes: [
			{
				type: 'page',
				pattern: /^\/$/,
				params: null,
				path: "/",
				a: [0,2],
				b: [1]
			},
			/*...*/
			]
```
This is created from `builder.generateManifest` ([link to impl](https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/blob/da29c3fb01b43674c9a824efcd983047ef8e488c/packages/kit/src/core/generate_manifest/index.js#L10)), and does *not* seem to include service workers.

I stumbled into the same issue  a few days ago. My current workaround is to add an additional `service-worker.js` into  folder `/static`, such that the generated service worker will be included in the final bundle.   

(Yes, **THE SERVICE WORKER** being served is compiled from `src/service-worker.ts` rather than `static/service-worker.js`)  

the demo: https://pwa-test-1mm.pages.dev/service-worker.js  
the repo: https://github.com/Envl/pwa-test    
Notice the code in `static/service-worker.js` is different from what that is in `src/service-worker.ts`. It seems what's inside  `static/service-worker.js` doesn't matter as long as it exists.

body:
Great to see work dedicated to this issue. Unfortunately, the update seems to have no effect - at least in the case of Cloudflare, which I was testing thoroughly (different browsers to avoid SW caching problems).

**Reproduction:**
I updated my initial demo site with a clean new version of the Sveltekit demo app.

When the service-worker.js file is included in /src _alone,_ the following error persists:

```
A bad HTTP response code (404) was received when fetching the script.
sw-cloudflare-repro.pages.dev/:1 Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Failed to register a ServiceWorker for scope ('https://sw-cloudflare-repro.pages.dev/') with script ('https://sw-cloudflare-repro.pages.dev/service-worker.js'): A bad HTTP response code (404) was received when fetching the script.

```
**But** I can confirm that the workaround proposed by @Envl is working also with the updated Sveltekit.

I added another copy of the service-worker.js file into the /static folder and console logged respectively to see which version is being used when deployed on Cloudflare.

I can confirm that the sheer existence of a service-worker.js file in the static folder somehow triggers the use of the SW, and it is     the one from /src and _not_ from /static.

So while the workaround seems valid also with the new version of Sveltekit, the issue unfortunately seems (at least on Cloudflare) not yet resolved.

### Describe the bug

This is in reference to #3187 and #3570

I decided to open a new issue regarding this topic, since #3570 does not solve the problem of `service-worker.js` not being bundled in case of `adapter-cloudflare`.

### Reproduction

I updated my initial demo site from #3187 with a clean new version of the Sveltekit demo app.

When the `service-worker.js` file is included in `/src` alone, the following error persists:

```
A bad HTTP response code (404) was received when fetching the script.
sw-cloudflare-repro.pages.dev/:1 Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Failed to register a ServiceWorker for scope ('https://sw-cloudflare-repro.pages.dev/') with script ('https://sw-cloudflare-repro.pages.dev/service-worker.js'): A bad HTTP response code (404) was received when fetching the script.
```

But I can confirm that the workaround proposed by @Envl is working also with the updated Sveltekit.

I added another copy of the `service-worker.js` file into the `/static` folder and console logged respectively to see which version is being used when deployed on Cloudflare.

I can confirm that the sheer existence of a `service-worker.js` file in the static folder somehow triggers the use of the SW, and it is the one from `/src` and not from `/static`.

So while the workaround seems valid also with the new version of Sveltekit, the issue itself unfortunately seems (at least on Cloudflare) not yet resolved.
